headline: Reuters explains that making data centers flexible about when they draw power could save US grids billions, but so far it has been tried mostly in pilot projects.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 6: fresh Reuters explainer on 8 Oct 2026; estimates are projections and the approach is largely untested at scale.
importance_line: Electricity bill payers could avoid some grid-upgrade costs and data centers could connect sooner, but flexibility is mostly untested at scale and one analyst warns that curtailment deals across hundreds of facilities need heavy spending and coordinated policy.
summary: Reuters reports that utilities and tech companies are increasingly exploring "demand response", in which data centers cut or shift electricity use when the grid is stressed, and that a Duke University study estimated greater flexibility could save 40 billion to 150 billion dollars in capital investment over the next decade. So far it has mostly been used in pilots and one-off deals, such as OpenAI's agreement to cut its grid draw by up to 1 gigawatt at a planned 3.2-gigawatt facility in Georgia, and experts say scaling it needs new tariffs, incentives and faster grid connection.
